name: Airlines
one_liner: Passenger and cargo air carriers with high fixed costs, volatile fuel expenses, and perishable inventory, where profit depends on filling seats at the right price.
how_it_makes_money: Airlines earn ticket revenue from passengers, plus ancillary fees (bags, seats, change fees) and cargo. Loyalty programs are a major profit center, with co-branded credit cards generating substantial high-margin revenue from banks buying miles.
revenue_formula: Passenger revenue = available seat miles (ASM) × load factor × yield
Revenue = passengers × average fare + ancillary revenue per passenger + cargo
cost_structure: Labor: often the largest cost, driven by union contracts
Fuel: often roughly 20-30% of operating costs, highly volatile
Aircraft ownership: leases, depreciation, and interest
Airport fees, landing charges, and navigation
margins: Airlines are historically low-margin and cyclical, with operating margins often in the low to high single digits and losses in downturns. Premium cabin mix, loyalty economics, network strength, and cost discipline separate the leaders from the rest.

key_metrics.name: Available seat miles (ASM)
key_metrics.what: Capacity, measured as seats flown times miles.

key_metrics.name: Load factor
key_metrics.what: Share of seats filled, a core efficiency metric.

key_metrics.name: Yield
key_metrics.what: Average fare per passenger mile, reflecting pricing power.

key_metrics.name: RASM / TRASM
key_metrics.what: Revenue per available seat mile, the key unit revenue metric.

key_metrics.name: CASM ex-fuel
key_metrics.what: Cost per available seat mile excluding fuel, the key unit cost metric.

key_metrics.name: On-time performance
key_metrics.what: Operational reliability, which affects customer satisfaction and costs.

trends: Premium cabin and loyalty revenue driving a split between strong network carriers and struggling low-cost carriers
Low-cost and ultra-low-cost carriers under pressure, with bankruptcies and consolidation
Aircraft delivery delays from Boeing and Airbus constraining capacity
Pilot and labor contract costs rising
Sustainable aviation fuel and decarbonization commitments
Air traffic control staffing and infrastructure challenges
